title: NCERT Grade 8 Mathematics | Perfect Squares
text:
Perfect Squares

Key terms: perfect square, odd factors

A perfect square is a number that can be expressed as the product of an integer with itself. For example, 4 is a perfect square because it can be expressed as 2 × 2. Perfect squares have an odd number of factors, which means they have a partner factor that, when multiplied together, gives the original number. For instance, 6 has factors 1, 2, 3, and 6, where 1 and 6 are a pair of partner factors.
